sm: The Supreme Court has put off deciding whether to dismiss the Cook County, Illinois, challenge to its ban on AR-15-style rifles as moot. In a brief unsigned order, it said it will defer the question until oral argument on Wednesday, December 2. The dispute began October 29, when lead plaintiff Cutberto Viramontes asked to be dismissed from the case without explanation, and the court granted that the day before. Cook County argued the case is moot because the other challenger, Christopher Khaya, wants an IMI Galil rifle, not an AR-15-style rifle. The challengers replied that the question covers similar rifles, and that Khaya also wants an AR-15 platform rifle. The order cited the 2023 case Acheson Hotels v. Laufer, but the court is more likely to reach the merits here because there are multiple plaintiffs and a companion challenge to Connecticut's ban.
